## Triage routing

**Labels** `bug` `tooling` `finding` `domain:devx` `pm:queue` `priority:p3` · **Type** Bug

**Lane — `domain:devx`.** `scripts/setup.sh` — the engineering face. Both defects and both fixes are in that one file.

**Re-measured on `83d4fda16` — both confirmed, with anchors.**

**Defect 1 — the hand-listed build chain**, `scripts/setup.sh:55, 58, 61, 64, 67, 70`:
```
pnpm --filter @object-ui/types build
pnpm --filter @object-ui/core build
pnpm --filter @object-ui/react build
pnpm --filter @object-ui/components build
pnpm --filter @object-ui/fields build
pnpm --filter @object-ui/layout build
```

**Defect 2 — `pnpm test:root` is not a script**, `scripts/setup.sh:75` — `if pnpm test:root; then`. I re-ran the card's measurement independently: `"test:root"` in the root `package.json` → **0 occurrences**. Confirmed undeclared.

**Admission — class (a) for defect 1** (reproducible failure on a clean checkout), **class (b) for defect 2** (a step that declares it runs tests and cannot).

---

## Grade p3, and the reason is the readers count

`git grep -l 'setup\.sh'` returns **only the root `README.md`**. No workflow runs it, so **CI cannot see either defect** — only a human following the README does. That caps the blast radius at "a new contributor's first hour", which is a real cost but a bounded and recoverable one.

Re-grade to p2 if `setup.sh` is ever referenced from a workflow, an onboarding doc beyond the README, or a skill — any of which turns a human-only trap into an automated one.

---

## ⭐ Defect 2 is the more interesting of the two, and it should not be treated as the small one

Because the call sits inside an `if`, it degrades to the `⚠ Some tests failed, but setup is complete` branch and **never surfaces as an error**. ⇒ the script's "run tests" step has been silently a no-op for as long as the script has been undeclared, while printing a message that reads as though tests ran and some failed.

That is worse than a hard failure in both directions: a contributor who sees the warning believes tests exist and are partly broken, and a contributor who does not read it believes tests passed. ⛔ Neither is true, and nothing distinguishes them. This is this repo's recurring shape — *a check that cannot fail is indistinguishable from one that passed* — here inverted into a check that cannot **run** while reporting that it did.

## Defect 1 — the class is already settled, so the fix shape is not open

The card's attribution is right and I am adopting it: this is the same defect class **objectui#7292** measured on `packages/components/package.json`'s `prebuild` — a hand-maintained copy of the dependency graph that drifts from the manifests turbo derives the real closure from. #7292's triage picked the fix shape (**delete the hand list, let `turbo run build` own the order**) and it applies verbatim here.

⚠️ **One provenance flag, stated because the card states it and it matters for who verifies what.** The failure reading — that under `set -e` the `pnpm --filter @object-ui/react build` step fails on a clean checkout with `TS2307: Cannot find module '@object-ui/i18n'` / `'@object-ui/data-objectstack'` — is **quoted from the #7292 dev, not re-measured by the filing seat**, and I have not re-measured it either. It is plausible and consistent with #7292's own finding, but ⛔ a claimant should reproduce it on a clean checkout before writing the fix rather than inheriting it. The *structural* claim (six hand-listed builds where turbo would derive the order) is measured and needs no re-check.

⚠️ Also recorded correctly by the card: **PR #7986 does not change this file's behaviour** — `setup.sh` already builds types/core/react itself, which is exactly what made the deleted `prebuild` redundant there. ⛔ Do not read #7986's landing as having fixed this.

---

## Disposition — I concur with the card: **one S-sized card, not two**

Replace the six-line chain with one `turbo run build` (or the documented `pnpm build`), and either point the test step at a script the root manifest declares or delete the step. Both edits are in one file with one reader, and splitting them would double the review for a file nothing gates.

⛔ On defect 2, **decide and state which**: pointing at a real script and deleting the step are materially different promises to a new contributor. If a script is chosen, name it in the claim comment; if the step is deleted, say so in the README's setup section too, so the document and the script agree.

**Dedup accepted as filed** and correctly controlled: a semantic search returned 0 issues at 06:40Z with a control query (the #7292 wording) returning #7292 first, so the zero is live rather than a dead channel.

**Refs:** #7292 (the manifest half of the class) · PR #7986 (its fix; ⛔ does not touch this file).

Triage seat only — no claim, no dispatch, no code.

## Why this card now — the total order, stated because the answer is counter-intuitive

The lane's written order is `priority:p0` > `pm:blocking` > `target:` > type **`Bug`** > the rest, tie-broken by **card age**. ⭐ Below `p0`, the priority label does **not** feature in that order. Re-derived at 10:53Z: no `p0`, **no `pm:blocking` at all**, no `target:` items ⇒ the live level is *type `Bug`*, and the queue holds 30 dispatchable cards it cannot empty this round ⇒ **oldest first**. This card is among the oldest Bugs in the lane.

⚠️ **One honest note on the card taken before this one.** objectui#8542 was claimed first and this seat called it "top of the total order" citing `priority:p1`. ⛔ Under the written order p1 does not rank; the justification that actually holds is a different rule — an advisory gate red on `main` is **shared damage**, to be stopped by whichever lane finds it. ⇒ Right card, ⛔ wrong reason given, corrected here.

⚠️ objectui#8380 is graded `p1` + `pm:queue` and is **already fixed** by `83d4fda16` (main's CI is green again; the proof is on that card). ⇒ Skipped by the premise check, ⛔ not dispatched.

⚠️ **Every fence, number and card status the brief carries is a PREDICTION.** ⛔ A zero-hit reading means nothing without a control term known present in the same run — **and without its exit code**: a probe this seat ran today returned exit 128 (`not a git repository`), which prints as no output and reads exactly like a clean zero.

⭐ **Filing rule:** a **concrete defect** carries **no labels at all**; an **observation** carries **`finding` only**. ⛔ Never a `domain:*`, ⛔ never an assignee.

**ACCEPT — PR #8560, one file, reviewed against the tree.** `domain:devx @ objectui` execution seat, PM session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`, R47, 2026-09-08T11:20Z. Head `7376a4c10`, base `3f775eeb8`, `scripts/setup.sh` **+57/-20**.

## Both halves, and the second one is repaired at the mechanism rather than the symptom

**Half 1** — the six-line hand-written build chain becomes one `pnpm build` (`turbo run build`), so the order comes from the manifests. The docblock carries the reproduction (`TS2307: Cannot find module '@object-ui/i18n'`, exit 2 on a clean checkout at `3f775eeb8`) and, more usefully, the reason it could never be kept correct by review: *"nothing tells the person adding a dependency that this file exists."*

**Half 2** — ⭐ this is the part worth the card. The brief warned that swapping in a name that happens to exist would repair the symptom and leave the mechanism. The dev did not do that. A new `require_root_script` helper **reads the script name back out of the root manifest** before invoking it, and both the build and the test step go through it.

The docblock states the mechanism exactly, and it is the interesting half:

> pnpm exits 254 on an unknown script — but that call sat inside an `if`, and an `if` condition **suppresses `set -e`**, so the miss took the else branch and printed "Some tests failed, but setup is complete".

⭐ *"A step that cannot run while reporting that it did is worse than one that fails: the contributor who reads the warning believes the suite exists and is partly broken, the one who does not believes it passed, and nothing distinguishes the two."* ⇒ The tolerant `else` survives on purpose but is now **bounded to genuine test failures**; an undeclared name can no longer reach it.

## ⭐ Non-vacuity, on the SHIPPED bytes

The guard was proven able to fail using the committed bytes — the function extracted from `scripts/setup.sh` with `sed`, ⛔ not re-typed — in **both** directions: a declared name (`test`) exits 0 silently; the old undeclared name (`test:root`) exits 1 with `setup.sh bug: root package.json declares no "test:root" script`. ⇒ A guard demonstrated to fire, ⛔ not asserted from its source.

## ⚠️ A falsified premise this seat passed on — verified here

The card and its triage comment both state that `git grep -l 'setup\.sh'` returns **only** the root `README.md`. Run verbatim on `origin/main` today it returns **7 files** (control in the same run: `pnpm` → 480, so the grep works):

```
README.md · scripts/__tests__/bash32-floor-wiring.test.ts
scripts/__tests__/shared-global-leak-guard.test.ts · scripts/__tests__/unit-registry-absence-collision.test.ts
vitest.config.mts · vitest.setup.shared-global-leak-guard.ts · vitest.setup.shared-global-leak.ts
```

Five are substring artefacts (`vitest.setup.shared-…`), but `bash32-floor-wiring.test.ts` is a **genuine** reference naming this file. ⚠️ **Three of the seven landed today** via objectui#8500 — so the filing seat's reading may have been true when written and drifted since. ⇒ Either way the corrected conclusion stands: **the file is not ungated.** `scripts/setup.sh` is inside `check:bash32-floor`'s population (its verdict counts "12 tracked shell file(s)") and that gate runs on pull requests. ⛔ Only its *runtime behaviour* is unseen by CI, ⛔ not the file. The `p3` grade survives; the grep quoted under it does not.

## The class-level fix was measured and declined, which is the right call

A repo-wide gate asserting every `pnpm SCRIPT` call in tracked shell against the manifest was **not** built, because the dev measured the population first: across all **12** tracked shell files, `setup.sh:75` was the class's **only** live instance. ⇒ ⭐ A gate for a set of size zero. ⛔ Declining it with the measurement is better than building it.

## ⚠️ A platform fact worth carrying forward — a dead search channel caught by a control

The dev's dedup ran into this: REST `/search/issues` is 403 here (known), so it fell back to MCP `search_issues` — which returned **0 for the target AND 0 for a control query using objectui#7987's own wording, while #7987 is open and indexed**. ⇒ ⭐ **That channel is dead and its zeros are not readings.** It then fell back to the REST *list* channel that had probed 200, fetched all 472 open non-PR issues across 5 pages, and grepped locally with a live control (`/setup\.sh/i` → #7987 and #8537 in the same run). ⛔ That is the only zero objectui#8559 was filed on.

## objectui#8559, and a trap this seat walked into while checking it

Filed correctly: ✔ **no labels at all**, ⛔ no assignee — a concrete defect, left for triage to grade.

⚠️ Verifying its premise, this seat first ran `git ls-tree origin/main --name-only ARCHITECTURE_EVALUATION.md` and read `$?` — which returned **0**, because `ls-tree` exits 0 whether or not the path matches. ⇒ The exit code was **not the signal**; only the empty output was. Re-done properly: `git ls-files --error-unmatch` exits **1** (control `README.md` exits 0), and `ls-tree` output line counts read **0 vs 1**. The file is genuinely untracked and `scripts/setup.sh` still points contributors at it. ⭐ Same family as the exit-128 zero earlier today: *a command that succeeds at finding nothing looks exactly like a command that failed to look.*

⇒ **ACCEPT.** Ready-flip, guard, queue and landing probe follow the CI verdict.

```

This one is the mirror image: a probe that returns a **hit it should not**, for the same reason the others returned a **zero they should not**.

## What is now on `main`

The six-line hand-written build chain is one `pnpm build`, so the order comes from the manifests — and the docblock records why the hand list could never be kept right by review: *"nothing tells the person adding a dependency that this file exists."*

⭐ And the half that matters more: `require_root_script` reads the script name **back out of the root manifest** before invoking it.
